  • A vase by ceramist Pol Chambost brings contrast to the table.
  • “I’d seen a few articles about Elza Wandler’s home and immediately thought: That’s exactly the kind of environment I want: creative, personal, and full of objects that tell stories,” Kroon recalls.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that “My previous home was dominated by shades of beige,” Jaco Kroon claims. “And it no longer suited me.” After a career in marketing, Kroon decided to head in a different direction and devote himself to a newly introduced creative pursuit: designing furniture for pets. He found the perfect setting for this fresh start in a 517-square-foot apartment in Amsterdam. Together with Elza Wandler, a designer and founder of her eponymous accessory brand, he created an interior that reflects his evolving vision. “I wanted a place that underscores my new direction—a more colorful, more creative, and more surprising home,” explains Kroon.

A vase by ceramist Pol Chambost brings contrast to the table.

“I’d seen a few articles about Elza Wandler’s home and immediately thought: That’s exactly the kind of environment I want: creative, personal, and full of objects that tell stories,” Kroon recalls. What began as creative interest soon developed into a friendship. During a lunch together in the designer’s garden, the two hit it off right away. In addition to their passion for interior design, they also share a love of dogs—they both own poodles.

It has been revealed that as Kroon got to know Wandler’s home better, he was particularly struck by the fact that every object had its own unique character. They wanted to create a similar atmosphere in his apartment, which led to a close creative collaboration in which they both contributed their ideas and visions. For Kroon, his home soon became more than just a place to live: “While the work was underway, I was developing my own line of pet furniture and realized just how much the new interior was influencing my creative work as well.”.

Sources indicate that jaco Kroon’s love for animals has come to shape his career. He’s seen here with his faithful toy poodle, Elio.

It has been revealed that the biggest challenge of the project was making the best use of the limited space. The 517-square-foot apartment combines a kitchen, living room, dining area, and sleeping area without feeling cramped or having to make any sacrifices. According to Wandler, the key was to view the spaces as a cohesive ecosystem: “In such small spaces, every single object interacts with the others. Even a four-inch-tall vase can completely alter the balance of a room.”.

Industry observers note that the bedroom is decorated in shades of salmon, with custom cabinets framing the bed. The wallpaper is by Kelly Wearstler. Wall sconces by Contain and the bedding is by Bonsoirs.

In a recent development, this gave rise to the project’s motto: “Every item must be a Beyoncé”—that’s how Wandler and Kroon jokingly describe their design philosophy. It’s their way of expressing the idea that every piece should bring its own personality and presence to the home without disrupting the harmony of the environment. The color scheme also follows this principle with intense yet carefully coordinated tones—such as the eggplant in the kitchen and the warm, velvety salmon pink in the bedroom—paired with textured woods, vintage fabrics, and custom details. “At first, the idea of a burgundy-violet kitchen really put me off,” Kroon admits with a smile. “But the further we got into the project, the more I felt my horizons expanding.”.

A blue bowl by Wandler x SolidNature and a ceramic basket by Ferm Living add splashes of color to the burgundy kitchen. The art on the wall is by Laura de Wilde.

One distinctive feature of the project is the interplay between functionality and aesthetics: Practical solutions blend so naturally into the design that they are barely recognizable as such at first glance. The historic Amsterdam townhouse, with its large windows, had very little storage space. That’s why Wandler took advantage of nearly every opportunity to create additional storage solutions. Custom cabinets frame the bed like an architectural backdrop, while the TV disappears into a specially designed piece of furniture made of zebrawood.

It has been revealed that “Elza has turned what would normally be a purely functional piece of furniture into something beautiful. She even convinced me to hide the TV behind the doors of a zebrawood cabinet!” jokes Kroon. “Everything seems to have been designed for aesthetic reasons, but in fact, every element is tailored to make optimal use of the available space.” The decision to use zebrawood also follows this philosophy: Its striking grain lends the interior a vertical dynamism and makes the room appear more spacious. “I wanted to use the wood to create movement and depth,” explains Wandler. “In a small room, you always have to consider how to increase the sense of space.”.

Recent findings suggest that colorful accents, such as the stool by Rutger de Regt, make a bold statement in the interior. The vase is by India Mahdavi and the sculpture on the wall is by Floor Merjenburgh.

Sources indicate that as is often the case with Wandler’s projects, restored vintage pieces, contemporary design, and works by young artists all find a place side by side here. The large vintage sofa was completely reupholstered, while the artwork and decorative pieces come from a network of emerging designers and artists supported by the designer through Kamer—her curatorial platform dedicated to collectible design.

The dark wood of the floor complements the chocolate-brown armchair by Norr11.

“It’s notable to me that I feel happy in my home,” notes Kroon. “And that it stimulates creativity.” Wandler sought to create this feeling through her selection of artwork and a carefully coordinated lighting design. The latter plays a central role in the living concept: Since the apartment faces multiple directions, the natural light changes constantly throughout the day, causing colors and materials to appear different depending on the time. This creates the impression that this small apartment was conceived as a place that evolves and can accompany personal transformation; it embraces newly introduced ideas, new ambitions, and new identities. “The greatest compliment,” Wandler concludes, “was when Jaco stated to me, ‘Now I feel like I’m finally living as the version of myself that I want to become.’”.

Sources indicate that the dining area, with a table from Westwing, is connected to the living room. The vintage sofa by Cini Boeri for Arflex has been reupholstered; the vase in front of the window is by l’Objet.

Electric truck operator Nevoya is expanding its deal with Meta with the fresh deployment of 25 Class 8 battery-electric trucks on the Interstate 10 (I-10) between San Bernardino, California and Phoenix, Arizona … but Meta won’t be shipping any products.

Recent findings suggest that the second major trucking deal between Facebook parent firm Meta and electric truck operator Nevoya will put 25 new battery-electric semis on I-10, running freight between San Bernardino, California and Phoenix, Arizona. But Meta isn’t buying trucks, hiring drivers or shipping its own products. Instead, Zuck’s company helping pay for someone else’s cleaner freight through environmental attribute certificates (EACs), a carbon credit mechanism that lets companies claim the emissions benefits of electric trucking without operating the trucks themselves.

According to recent reports, “Coming back to Nevoya for a second corridor reflects what we look for in our value chain work: partners that can scale, and agreements we can repeat, said Devon Lake, Head of Net Zero Strategy, Meta. “Freight is part of the emissions footprint of building and operating our data centers, and multi-year commitments like this help address our scope 3 emissions and make electric trucking available and competitive on the routes that serve the regions where we build.”.

It has been revealed that meta was one of several buyers in the DC-based Center for Green Market Activation (GMA) buyers’ alliance. The group’s collective EAC purchases supported Nevoya’s initial 63-truck deployment on the Houston–Dallas corridor back in May. This new Agreement, however, is a standalone deal between Nevoya and Meta only, and gives Meta an established framework to open more electric truck corridors in the future.

This clever application of these agreements is what makes the Dallas-Houston run stand out, with GMA calling it, “the first large-scale application of book and claim to zero-emission trucking.” The manufacturer adds that this arrangement helps client companies overcome existing barriers to EV adoption while enabling Nevoya to deploy new trucks, “where they deliver the strongest commercial and operational value.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bitcoin is trading just above its realized price, the average cost of every coin on the network, and a break below that level would put the average holder at a loss for the first time since early 2023, Glassnode, an onchain analytics firm posted Friday.
  • It has been revealed that the price of bitcoin sat near $61,700 on Friday after sliding below $62,000.
  • The firm said the MVRV ratio, which compares bitcoin’s market value with its realized value, sits “just above 1.” A reading of 1 means the market price has fallen all the way to the realized price.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin is trading just above its realized price, the average cost of every coin on the network, and a break below that level would put the average holder at a loss for the first time since early 2023, Glassnode, an onchain analytics firm posted Friday.

It has been revealed that the price of bitcoin sat near $61,700 on Friday after sliding below $62,000. The realized price is a measure of what holders paid, not where the market trades. When bitcoin trades above it, the typical coin is sitting on a gain. Below it, the typical coin is underwater.

The margin is thin. The firm said the MVRV ratio, which compares bitcoin’s market value with its realized value, sits “just above 1.” A reading of 1 means the market price has fallen all the way to the realized price.

Industry observers note that realized price values each coin at the price it last moved on the blockchain, then averages across the supply. Look Into Bitcoin describes it as bitcoin’s average cost basis. Because it tracks the price when coins last changed hands, it moves far more slowly than the market.

In a recent development, the MVRV ratio expresses the same idea as a multiple. Above 1, holders are in profit on average. Below 1, they are not. A reading just above 1 means the market price is only a sliver higher than what the average coin cost.

In a recent development, the firm did not give the exact realized price in its post, which included a chart. That leaves the exact cushion between today’s price and the average cost basis unstated. Bitcoin Magazine Pro’s full realized price chart sits behind a login, so the current level could not be confirmed independently for this report.

Recent findings suggest that “The average Bitcoin holder is still in profit,” the firm wrote. “The margin is thin.”.

The slide has come with heavy selling from funds. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) lost about $541 million on Thursday, its largest one-day outflow since it debuted in January 2024, Bloomberg reported. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $582 million in total that day.

It has been revealed that the selling stands out against the buying earlier in the fall. Institutions piled into bitcoin ETFs through the third quarter, pushing their combined holdings to a record, Bitcoin Magazine reported this week.

It has been revealed that leveraged traders took losses too. More than $700 million in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, and about 86% of them were bets on higher prices. Bitcoin accounted for roughly $200 million of the total.

CoinShares head of research James Butterfill said the drop is part of a longer downturn rather than the start of a fresh one. “I see this as a continuation of the existing bear market rather than the start of another,” he said in a note dated Nov. 18.

According to recent reports, the note frames Friday’s price action as a late stage of a decline that began well before November. Butterfill pointed to whale selling that weighed on prices from late 2025, expectations of higher interest rates and weakness in technology stocks, all of which have kept buyers cautious.

In a recent development, “Our base case remains range trading around USD 60k to 90k through much of 2027, until falling inflation gives monetary policy room to ease,” he said. “Geopolitics will have a considerable say in that.”.

A move through the realized price would put bitcoin near the bottom edge of that range. The firm said holders as a group have not been in loss since early 2023.

A sustained breakout, Butterfill mentioned, would likely require “a change in the policy outlook, renewed whale participation or both.”.

Breaking: Can You Lose 10 Pounds In A Month? Experts Share 15 Tips For Safe Weight Loss In 30 Days

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1734 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Womenshealthmag

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It only makes sense to want to give your weight loss journey everything you’ve got.
  • Here's the truth: The average person cannot safely lose 10 pounds in a month, claims Michael Glickman, MD, a board-certified family medicine and obesity medicine physician and founder of Revolution Medicine, Health and Fitness.
  • According to recent reports, meet the experts: Michael Glickman, MD, is a board-certified family medicine and obesity medicine physician and founder of Revolution Medicine, Health and Fitness.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It only makes sense to want to give your weight loss journey everything you’ve got. And, if you’re into big goals, you may wonder if it’s safe to lose 10 pounds in a month.

Here's the truth: The average person cannot safely lose 10 pounds in a month, claims Michael Glickman, MD, a board-certified family medicine and obesity medicine physician and founder of Revolution Medicine, Health and Fitness. Losing weight at this aggressive of a pace can raise your risk of developing gallstones (painful deposits of digestive fluid in the gallbladder) and up the odds that you’ll regain the weight down the line, he says. (Neither of those are ideal!).

According to recent reports, meet the experts: Michael Glickman, MD, is a board-certified family medicine and obesity medicine physician and founder of Revolution Medicine, Health and Fitness. Michael Hamlin, CSCS, is a certified strength and conditioning specialist and the founder of Everflex Fitness.

Of course, everyone is different and a lot depends on your starting weight. Also, you can still have aggressive goals when it comes to weight loss—it’s just that 10 pounds in a too-short timeframe is a tricky benchmark for most people. So, how much weight can you safely lose in a month—and how should you even go about it? Here’s what experts suggest.

In a recent development, the timeline will be different for everyone, given factors like starting weight, genetics, nutrition, activity level, stress, and more. But Dr. Glickman states to give yourself anywhere from two to three months to hit that 10-pounds-lost goal. “For some, this could take longer, so be compassionate with your body and prioritize what’s best for your health,” he says.

In a recent development, when it comes to how much weight is safe to lose at a given time, stick to one to two pounds per week, says Dr. Glickman. “Some people can shed weight more promptly in the first month after instituting a lower calorie and healthy diet, however much of the weight loss on the scale will have been due to water weight.”.

If you have obesity and are revamping your eating habits, along with starting an exercise program after being fairly sedentary, you may see bigger gains early on than someone with a lower starting weight who isn’t making drastic changes.

First things first: A safe way to lose weight is a holistic and multi-factorial approach that involves optimal nutrition, frequent exercise, stress reduction, and adequate sleep, indicates Dr. Glickman. It's not necessarily about eating less but being conscious of the diversity of plants in your diet, and the avoidance of processed foods, refined oils, and refined carbohydrates, he explains.

According to recent reports, on top of that, apply sustainable healthy changes to your routine that you enjoy, claims Michael Hamlin, CSCS, a certified strength and conditioning specialist and the founder of Everflex Fitness. Maybe that means attending a workout class with friends twice a week, cooking a plant-based dinner with your partner, or throwing on your favorite podcast and going for a solo walk.

Sources indicate that sleep deprivation promotes an increase in ghrelin, your hunger hormone, which can trigger late night snacking, ultimately increasing your daily caloric intake, says Dr. Glickman. So do your best to get seven to nine hours of sleep per night. Not only that, getting more sleep helps you feel more energized, so you can add more activity to your day.

Recent findings suggest that it may sound simple, but 30 minutes of daily walking can do wonders, says Dr. Glickman. “It isn’t about calorie burning—it’s about the mobility, the happy hormones your brain releases, and the physiological anti-inflammatory responses that have long-term impacts on your weight.”.

Getting daily steps in has health benefits ranging from lowering your risk of developing type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease to helping you live longer. While any movement is good, moving at a brisk pace is the best way to get in all those extra perks.

Plant diversity has been shown to have the most beneficial impact on the gut microbiome, which influences your metabolic set point (the body’s preferred weight), insulin levels, and fat storage, says Dr. Glickman. Plant-based diets are also linked to a lower risk of developing heart disease, stroke, and diabetes, making this a big win for your overall health, too.

His suggestion? Try a plant-based day or meal per week to ensure you’re supporting your gut microbiome and loading up on the veggies.

Recent findings suggest that it’s best to consult a doctor or registered dietitian to determine your daily caloric needs since it depends on your age, gender, activity level, muscle mass, current weight, and the amount of calories you burn at rest (a.k.a. your basal metabolic rate), says Hamlin. From there, they can determine a slight calorie deficit, or how many calories you need in a day to lose one to two pounds a week, he explains.

While you’re waiting for a consult, check out the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases’ online body weight planner. It asks you to enter some basic information like your current weight, your ideal weight, and your activity level, and provides what your daily calorie goals should be to help you get there.

Industry observers note that “Stress can lead to increased hunger hormones and an elevated metabolic set point,” says Dr. Glickman. Higher levels of the stress hormone cortisol can create stubborn fat distribution around the abdomen, he adds.

It has been revealed that although this one is often easier said than done, to help combat stress and anxiety, try relaxation techniques like meditation, yoga, and journaling. And, of course, if you’re struggling with stress management, consider reaching out to a mental health therapist for individual guidance on navigating everything.

“Sometimes we can mistake the feeling of thirst for hunger, so make sure to stay hydrated throughout the day, especially during and after exercise,” Dr. Glickman says. Women should drink about 11.5 cups (2.7 liters) of fluids a day, per Mayo Clinic. (Note: That total can come from food and liquids.).

Strength training has a significant impact on your metabolism and fat burning capabilities, studies show, so incorporate resistance training at least three days a week, claims Dr. Glickman. Just take note that because strength training builds muscle, you may notice little or even no overall weight change at times, even though you are losing fat. (Not sure where to start with your strength training journey? Try Women's Health's The Woman's Guide To Strength Training: Dumbbells.).

HIIT workouts burn a ton of calories and can change your body composition while building muscle, says Hamlin. In fact, women who incorporated HIIT programming achieved similar body composition and aerobic capacity results in half the time as women who did moderate-intensity workouts, a 2017 study published in the Journal of Diabetes Research found.

Sources indicate that fiber helps regulate blood sugar levels, prevent insulin resistance and diabetes, and is an excellent source of nutrition for healthy bacteria in the gut, claims Dr. Glickman. High-fiber foods like vegetables are also filling without overloading on the calories, explains Hamlin. You can get fiber in powder or supplement form, but your best (and healthiest) bet is from plants, adds Dr. Glickman.

Industry observers note that weight gain is linked with the consumption of highly processed and packaged foods, Dr. Glickman claims. “This includes any food item in a wrapper with ingredients you can’t pronounce, even if the calories and carbohydrates seem appealing,” he explains. “Always choose whole foods over packaged ones.”.

Do your best to prioritize cooking at home to eliminate sneaky fats, sugars, and processed ingredients that are not listed on a menu, claims Dr. Glickman.

Focus on the quality of food on your plate and aim for three hearty meals a day that include a small amount of complex carbohydrates (root veggies and whole grains), a moderate amount of high-quality protein (fish, chicken, eggs, and tofu), and lots of plant-based fiber, says Dr. Glickman.

Alcoholic drinks lack nutritional value and are usually packed with calories, so it’s best to scale back on booze, claims Hamlin. When you drink alcohol, it also immediately goes to the liver where it’s prioritized as an energy source, so your body burns alcohol cals first. Not only that, alcohol also lowers your inhibitions and raises the odds you’ll eat more than you need to feel satiated.

To help with accountability, Hamlin suggests using a food journal or app to track your meals. This will give you a better understanding and awareness of how many calories you’re consuming and at which meal. Research shows this is an effective way to lose weight, too. One study found that people who tracked their meals at least five days of each week had “significant and sustained weight loss” over time compared to people who tracked less or inconsistently.

Recent findings suggest that it can take time for your stomach to recognize when it’s full, so pause in between portions before deciding if you actually want more, states Hamlin. You can either pre-pack your meals with smaller portion sizes or use smaller plates to provide a visual cue. One scientific analysis of 14 studies found that people who ate smaller portions had a “substantial” drop in how many calories they ate each day.

Think long-term about weight loss and establish a goal that is realistic for your lifestyle, says Hamlin. Your goals might take time and patience, but that’s okay, he adds. “Weight loss isn't solely about a caloric deficit, because the body is a super complex piece of machinery, and we can't simply boil all of weight loss down to calories in versus calories out.”.

#64313. Tech Report: Elvis Presley at Home: Tour the King’s Private Life in 14 Photos, From the Heartland to Hawaii

Tech Report: Elvis Presley at Home: Tour the King’s Private Life in 14 Photos, From the Heartland to Hawaii

📅 19 May 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1968 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Architecturaldigest

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Elvis Presley is one of those icons so permanently etched into the fabric of American popular culture that it seems, nearly half a century after his death, as if he will live forever.
  • Recent findings suggest that today, the museum, which encompasses Presley’s gravesite, former home, and a collection of mementos of Presley’s rock-and-roll career, stands as a stirring reminder of one man’s life, as he grew from a beloved child to poverty-stricken parents to, arguably, the most famous man in the world.
  • Presley and his parents pose for a photo at home in Tupelo, Mississippi, circa 1945—the year before he received his first guitar.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Elvis Presley is one of those icons so permanently etched into the fabric of American popular culture that it seems, nearly half a century after his death, as if he will live forever. While Presley also had homes in California, and famously lived in Germany during his stint in the US Army, it is Graceland that is most strongly associated with the late musician. The rock and roller’s Memphis residence where he lived for 20 years and where he died at the age of 42, Graceland is America’s second-most-visited residence, behind the White House. Every year, an average of 600,000 people flock to the residence turned museum, which opened to the public in 1982.

Recent findings suggest that today, the museum, which encompasses Presley’s gravesite, former home, and a collection of mementos of Presley’s rock-and-roll career, stands as a stirring reminder of one man’s life, as he grew from a beloved child to poverty-stricken parents to, arguably, the most famous man in the world. Below, we’re rounding up photos of the legendary musician at his (almost) equally famous home, and other places he rested his pompadoured head.

The Presleys at home in Tupelo, around 1945.

Presley and his parents pose for a photo at home in Tupelo, Mississippi, circa 1945—the year before he received his first guitar. The future king of rock and roll was born nearby, in a two-room house built by his father, grandfather, and uncle on January 8, 1935. That house, now a museum, was repossessed three years later, and the family bounced around other homes in the area before moving to Memphis when Presley was 13 years old. There, the family lived in Lauderdale Courts, a public housing project.

Presley relaxing at 1034 Audubon Drive.

It has been revealed that in March 1956, riding high on the success of Presley’s first RCA single, “Heartbreak Hotel,” the family became homeowners for the very first time. A house of her own had always been Gladys’s dream, and her 21-year-old son made it a reality when he paid $29,250 for 1034 Audubon Drive, a low-rise, seven-room ranch house with four bedrooms. Gladys likened it to living in a palace. They also added a backyard pool–at the time, it was the only one on the street. While most wealthy men of his tender age might have set their parents up with a house before shimmying off to live the bachelor’s life elsewhere, this wasn’t Elvis’s style; living together as a close-knit trio was always part of his master strategy.

Elvis Presley and a friend chat in the back yard of his house at 1034 Audubon Drive in 1956.

On their quiet, leafy street in the rapidly growing East Memphis, the Presleys were soon living the suburban dream. Things might well have stayed that way too, had Elvis’s star not reached stratospheric heights over the following months. By the summer of 1956, Elvis had recorded smash hits “Hound Dog” and “Don’t Be Cruel.” His first feature film, Love Me Tender, premiered later that year, making him a bona fide movie star.

Swarms of fans soon crowded the sidewalk outside the family home day and night. Elvis had initially slept in the front bedroom, which was decorated with pink floral wallpaper, but eventually moved into the master bedroom at the back of the house after fans began peering through his window for a glimpse of their idol. To restore some shred of privacy, the Presleys had a brick and metal fence installed around the property. Elvis is pictured above leaning against the railings, chatting to a friend in his backyard.

Elvis and his parents relax on the patio.

Elvis kicks his feet up alongside his parents on the Audubon Drive home’s patio in this July 1956 photo. The Presleys had moved to this upper-middle-class neighborhood just four months prior. During their residency, the family tried to fit in with their neighbors in the affluent community to the best of their ability; Gladys let local kids cool off in their newly installed pool and made them peanut butter sandwiches, while Elvis would take them for a spin on the back of his gleaming motorcycle. But it soon became clear that Elvis’s fame would put a strain on life in the area. Perhaps it was when Hollywood star Natalie Wood came to stay at the house on Audubon—which turned the street into a circus as fans gathered to watch her pose outside on Elvis’s motorcycle—or the hot dog stand that set up outside that magically appeared to feed the constant stream of fans. The final straw may have been when a helicopter landed on the vacant lot beside the house to collect Elvis, leaving the neighbors well and truly shaken up.

Recent findings suggest that by March 1957 the Presleys had packed their bags and moved on from the house on Audubon, restoring a relative sense of peace to the quaint suburban neighborhood. The family may have spent just a year at their Audubon Drive home, but it was a pivotal chapter in Elvis’s life story, marking a transition between the transient lifestyle of his impoverished childhood and the security and permanence he would find in his next home: Graceland.

The upcoming homeowner with his hand on one of Graceland’s now iconic columns.

Industry observers note that presley skyrocketed to stardom in the mid ’50s, garnering a recording contract with RCA Records. This newfound wealth meant the boy whose home was repossessed, and who lived in public housing, could now buy the lavish house of his dreams for himself and his parents. In March 1957, the 22-year-old “Hound Dog” singer paid $102,500 for Graceland, which would remain his primary residence for the rest of his life. The home had been built in 1939 on a plot of land the original owner named after his daughter, Grace; the name stuck. Here, Presley leans on one of the home’s pillars shortly after the purchase.

Elvis in wrought iron, and in the flesh, at the gates to Graceland.

The musician poses in front of Graceland’s famous wrought iron music note gate in April 1957, around the time he had it installed. Abe Saucer designed the gates—which feature life-size images of Elvis playing guitar amid musical notes—and had them custom-built by John Dillars Jr. At the time, the property spanned 13.8 acres, with the mansion clocking in at over 10,200 square feet—later, Elvis would expand it to 17,500 square feet and 23 rooms, with additions including the famous Jungle Room.

A palace fit for the king of rock and roll.

The “Burning Love” singer walks in front of Graceland, circa 1957. Early design details that Presley added to the Colonial Revival estate included a custom 15-foot-long blue metallic sofa (later reupholstered in white), a pink flagstone wall around the property, a kidney-shaped swimming pool, and a full-size soda fountain. In his initial renovations, Presley spent $500,000 (over $5 million in today’s dollars).

Recent findings suggest that in March 1958, Presley was drafted into the US Army. He is pictured in his off-post home in Bad Nauheim, Germany, in January 1960, shortly after being promoted to sergeant. It was here that the 24-year-old singer met a 14-year-old Priscilla Beaulieu, when a friend of his who had spotted Priscilla at a restaurant brought her to a party at Presley’s place to introduce them. To this day, the home at 14 Goethestrasse is still a landmark for fans.

Elvis and his father mourning after the death of Gladys.

Elvis and his father Vernon on the steps of Graceland in August 1958, shortly after the deathof his beloved mother, Gladys. The two had been exceptionally close, and her loss was toprove a devastating turning point. Elvis had always believed that the purpose of his extraordinary success was to provide his parents with the security and comfort they had been denied during his childhood. Buying them a home, and ultimately one as grand as Graceland, had been central to that vision. But now, just as he had achieved everything he had worked for, his mother was gone. With the loss of her unwavering love and support, it was as though a curtain had fallen on Elvis’s life. The young man who had once seemed so certain of his place in the world would never quite be the same again.

In a recent development, in March, 1960, Presley was discharged from the Army and returned home to Graceland, but it was a sadder and lonelier place, since Gladys died while he was in basic training. Here, he stands with his Rolls-Royce in front of Graceland, circa 1960. The Jailhouse Rock star had an affinity for slick cars, but it wasn’t the only mode of transportation he enjoyed at the estate. Priscilla Beaulieu, who came to visit him at Graceland in 1962 and moved in the following year, wrote in her 1985 memoir Elvis and Me that he “turned Graceland into a private playground for us all. He’d have gun-shooting contests and also ‘screaming thrill rides’ when he’d pack several people into his custom-built golf cart and race around the grounds at top speed.”.

Elvis and Priscilla were married in Las Vegas on May 1, 1967. He was 32; she was 21. Exactly nine months later, on February 1, 1968, their first and only child, Lisa Marie Presley, was born.

Priscilla and Elvis brought a tropical design aesthetic home from their vacations in Hawaii.

According to recent reports, hawaii became a bit of a home away from home for Presley following his 1961 film, Blue Hawaii. He returned often to vacation there, including in 1968, when this snapshot was taken. The “Don’t Be Cruel” singer was so inspired by the tropical locale that he added a tiki-inspired space to Graceland. Now known as the Jungle Room, the kitschy den features wood-paneled walls, green shag carpeting on the floor and ceiling, carved wooden furniture with faux fur upholstery, and a built-in rock waterfall feature.

Priscilla, Elvis, and baby Lisa Marie relax at home.

Industry observers note that the Presleys relax in Graceland’s pool area, circa 1970. He had added the kidney-shaped pool and flagstone patio to the property in 1957. This snapshot shares a relaxed, happy moment, but life with Elvis wasn’t all pool parties for Priscilla. In Elvis and Me, Priscilla wrote frankly about their controversial relationship: “When we met, I had just turned 14. The first six months I spent with him were filled with tenderness and affection. Blinded by love, I saw none of his faults or weaknesses. He was to become the passion of my life. He taught me everything: how to dress, how to walk, how to apply makeup and wear my hair, how to behave, how to return love—his way. Over the years he became my father, husband, and very nearly God.”.

Lisa Marie and her father at Graceland.

Sources indicate that elvis and Lisa Marie are shown here on the porch of Graceland in the early 1970s. Lisa Marie later recalled the curious rhythms of life at the mansion. Her father was nocturnal, she explained, and the household rarely got going before about two in the afternoon. Lisa Marie remembered fondly hearing the rotary phone ring and being summoned upstairs to spend quality time with her dad in his bedroom. “I would just sit up there, and he’d talk to me and ask what I was doing while he watched one of his 17 televisions or listened to records,” she said in her memoir, From Here to the Great Unknown, co-written with her daughter Riley Keough. On occasion, Elvis would come downstairs and take the family and their friends out for an impromptu evening at the movie theater, shutting it down so they could watch a James Bond film or The Pink Panther.

#64311. Block Notes Most Bitcoin Payments on Square Are for Coffee and Food

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (639 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Bitcoinmagazine ↗ Open Full Page

Block Notes Most Bitcoin Payments on Square Are for Coffee and Food

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (639 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bitcoinmagazine

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Most bitcoin payments at Square sellers are small, everyday purchases at coffee shops and restaurants, Block stated in a fresh report that it hopes will inform a debate in Congress over a tax break for small crypto purchases.
  • The report, “The State of Bitcoin Payments,” covers completed bitcoin payments at U.S.
  • Food and drink businesses took 72% of those payments, Block found.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Most bitcoin payments at Square sellers are small, everyday purchases at coffee shops and restaurants, Block stated in a fresh report that it hopes will inform a debate in Congress over a tax break for small crypto purchases.

The report, “The State of Bitcoin Payments,” covers completed bitcoin payments at U.S. Square sellers from Nov. 1, 2025, to Oct. 15, 2026. The median payment was about $13, and the average was about $29.

Food and drink businesses took 72% of those payments, Block found. That is a bigger share than the category’s 67.5% slice of regular card payments on Square over the same period.

“Most bitcoin payments are small and routine,” the firm wrote on X Thursday, calling the report one of the first datasets on how people spend bitcoin in the local economy.

It has been revealed that coffee shops and fast food businesses accounted for 62.6% of the bitcoin payments in the food and drink category, with a median payment of $9.10. Grocery stores made up a smaller share but had the highest average payment in the group, at $60.73.

According to recent reports, small tickets dominated. About 42% of bitcoin payments on Square were under $10, and 65.1% were under $20. Those sub-$20 payments made up just 19.1% of total payment value, though, with a few larger purchases accounting for much of the dollars spent.

In a recent development, customers also came back. Among Cash App users who paid with bitcoin at least twice at the same merchant, the median was three purchases per customer-merchant pair. About 44% of bitcoin payments from Cash App were repeat payments, and 86% of those came within 30 days.

The activity was not limited to Block’s own app. External Lightning wallets such as Strike, Wallet of Satoshi, Phoenix and Coinbase handled 56.6% of Square bitcoin payments and about 66% of payment value, while Cash App wallets made up the rest.

According to recent reports, square sellers can choose how much of each sale they keep in bitcoin, and Square converts the rest to dollars automatically. Block remarked zero-fee processing for bitcoin payments on Square has been extended through Dec. 31, 2027. Local governments are testing similar setups, with Miami-Dade County now taking bitcoin for property taxes and converting it to dollars.

Block tied the data to tax policy. Under current U.S. federal rules, paying with bitcoin generally means calculating a capital gain or loss on every purchase, even a $10 coffee, the company mentioned.

A Morning Consult survey that Block commissioned found that 23.6% of businesses that don’t accept bitcoin cite tax and accounting complexity as a reason. That is about the same share that cite regulation, refunds or price swings. Among businesses that have considered taking bitcoin but haven’t, the figure was 27%.

Consumers pointed to friction, too. Morning Consult surveyed 8,669 U.S. adults who are aware of bitcoin in August. Among those who don’t own it, 29.6% stated they would be more likely to pay with bitcoin if it were easier, and 15.7% of that group said they were unsure how it is taxed or regulated.

It has been revealed that block remarked Congress is weighing a crypto tax package and pointed to a de minimis exemption, which would exempt small gains on qualifying purchases, as one option. Industry groups have pressed lawmakers on crypto tax rules for months, with little movement so far.

According to recent reports, the report doesn’t give totals. Block said the number of Square bitcoin payments, the number of sellers receiving them and total bitcoin payment volume are proprietary and not disclosed. Merchant lists like the 425 Los Angeles businesses that accept bitcoin offer a rough sense of reach.

“We think tax policy should account for how people spend bitcoin as well as how they hold it,” Block said.

Latest Update: I Found the 11 Best Running Shoes for Women for Every Type of Run

📅 07 Dec 2023 | ⏱️ 19 min read (3784 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Womenshealthmag

⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • LOW-IMPACT EXERCISES might be forever buzzy, but the running community is going stronger than ever.
  • As a former competitive runner who still throws down high mileage (50 to 60 miles weekly), I’ve learned the right footwear is crucial for allowing you to continue to pound the pavement, and selecting the right kind of running shoe is crucial, too.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

LOW-IMPACT EXERCISES might be forever buzzy, but the running community is going stronger than ever. From 5Ks to marathons, lots of women are lacing up to go for a run and getting all the physical and mental health benefits that come with it. Data suggests running is great for everything from cardiovascular fitness to a healthier mindset, and it may even lower your risk of eight major diseases, making it a solid fitness habit to get into. And then there’s the fact that running makes you feel like you’ve accomplished something amazing (because you have).

As a former competitive runner who still throws down high mileage (50 to 60 miles weekly), I’ve learned the right footwear is crucial for allowing you to continue to pound the pavement, and selecting the right kind of running shoe is crucial, too. The best running shoes for women provide support and cushioning, with the perfect level of fit to help you forget about your footwear while you run.

Industry observers note that while you can skimp on some fitness gear, a quality pair of running shoes is an key investment, according to Melissa Lockwood, DPM, a podiatrist at Heartland Foot and Ankle Associates in Bloomington, Illinois “I am very much in the camp of paying for a really good pair of running shoes,” she states. “It can help really minimize injury in the future.” (Still, if you’re on a tight budget or just want to save a buck, these are our favorite cheap running shoes.).

Industry observers note that but, before taking the plunge on racking up miles, it’s vital to figure out what kind of heel-to-toe drop, toe box, stability, cushioning, and heel stack is best for you. Finding the perfect running shoes involves understanding how specific design elements impact your comfort, performance, and overall experience.

There is no right or wrong, as everyone has different needs (and those needs for running shoes differ from walking shoes), but we'll go over the most important factors to consider when shopping for running shoes.

It has been revealed that hoka does it right when it comes to a durable, high-quality shoe—specifically the Clifton 11, which was released in July 2026 in tandem with the higher-performance-oriented Clifton Pro. The Clifton family has been a crowd pleaser in the running community and amongst WH editors for a long time, and with good reason.

Recent findings suggest that the Clifton 11 is considered one of the brand’s most versatile running shoes, making it a good fit for everyone from beginners to seasoned pros. WH style editor Shannon Zitz notes her feet never felt fatigued while she was testing this shoe, even with plantar fasciitis. “There’s technically a rocker shape built into the sole, but it's subtle enough that I barely noticed it—instead, my stride just felt smooth and natural whether I was walking or running,” she says.

Industry observers note that the Clifton 11 has an eight-millimeter heel-to-toe drop to help alleviate pressure on the plantar fascia, and the brand shaved off almost half an ounce from the weight of the model’s previous version, the Clifton 10, primarily through weight-saving revisions to the shoe’s upper. This was the primary change, with Hoka keeping the midsole that we know and love the same.

Recent findings suggest that these shoes offer maximum cushioning you’ll feel—the same EVA foam found in the Bondi 9 without the extra bulk. Just be aware that these don’t offer any stability innovations for flat feet, which is especially essential if you’re prone to overpronation. As for fit, the toe box does run narrow, but luckily, wide sizing is available.

Recent findings suggest that read More: Hoka Clifton 11 vs. Hoka Clifton Pro.

Industry observers note that on has built an empire out of its highly cushioned Cloudmonster line. But its most cushioned shoe of all is the Cloudmonster 3 Hyper, an impressively bouncy sneaker that’ll make you feel like a gazelle bounding down the street.

It’s generally accepted that the more cushioning a shoe has, the heavier its weight (because of all that foam packed into the midsole). But the On Cloudmonster 3 Hyper manages to deliver a highly cushioned shoe in a relatively lightweight 7.5 oz package. The result is a next-level energy return that feels like it’s propelling you forward with each step.

Sources indicate that this sneaker has a soft, breathable upper to minimize foot sweat, along with a highly padded heel collar that lowers the risk of rubbing. I’ve worn a lot of running shoes, and that heel collar may be the thickest I’ve ever seen. There’s a nice, roomy toe box, too.

Sources indicate that while there’s a lot to love about the Cloudmonster 3 Hyper, it’s not perfect. This shoe’s $220 price tag puts it out of reach for many, and the tongue is on the thin side (not a deal-breaker, but some people prefer something more padded). Still, if you have the budget for it and like to feel like you’re running on actual clouds, this is a solid choice.

Read More: Best On Walking Shoes.

According to recent reports, think of a daily trainer as the chameleon of the running shoe world. This sneaker needs to be able to be durable enough for regular use, comfortable, and versatile enough to handle higher mileage along with speedier runs. The Adidas Adizero Evo SL was designed with all of that in mind, serving up a highly adaptable shoe that works for nearly everyone. That’s probably why this shoe keeps landing on the feet of runners all over the place.

It has been revealed that the Adizero Evo SL has a soft, bouncy feel underfoot and plenty of energy return thanks to Adidas’ proprietary Lightstrike Pro foam packed into the midsole. It’s also relatively lightweight, clocking in at just under 8 oz. The shoe’s peppy sensation and slight rocker shape support your stride but don’t push you forward in a way that feels unnatural.

According to recent reports, this sneaker has an engineered mesh upper to let your feet breathe, even when you’re clocking some serious mileage. This shoe has a slightly tapered toe box, which isn’t for everyone. The outsole is also a little flat and isn’t the grippiest you’ll find, but road runners are unlikely to have an issue. While you’re probably not choosing a running shoe based on looks alone, it doesn’t hurt that the Adizero Evo SL looks sleek.

It has been revealed that the best shoe for recovery runs is a total workhorse, delivering enough stability and cushioning to keep you comfortable as you move along at a moderate pace. The Brooks Ghost Max 3 is up for the challenge, with a wide, stable base and supportive feel to take the pressure off your joints.

Recent findings suggest that this isn’t a stability shoe, per se—it won’t work to correct your stride—but it still creates a sense like you’re not going to roll an ankle or have any other gait challenges as you pound the pavement. The Ghost Max 3 is a heavier shoe, although I haven’t noticed any fatigue or extra drag in it. But this sneaker holds up well to high-volume running. I wear this regularly and have never noticed any durability issues.

The Ghost Max 3 features nitrogen-infused DNA Loft v3 foam for support and cushioning. However, it won’t give you a sinking-in feel and there is limited energy return, which could be a pro or con, depending on what you’re after. This sneaker also has a jacquard mesh upper that feels a little softer than many other running shoes out there. The Ghost Max 3 provides plenty of room, from the midfoot to the toe box, making it a good fit for people with wider feet. Just don’t strategy to do any speed work in this shoe—it’s a little too heavy for that.

Read More: Brooks Ghost Max 3 Review.

In a recent development, it's clear that Lululemon’s Wildfeel was designed by people who actually do trail running. It has features you want in a trail running shoe beyond just good grip.

There’s a knitted sock-like upper that molds to your foot to keep out pebbles and other debris, along with a toe bumper to protect your feet over rugged terrain. I took these shoes on several runs over a rocky trail near my house, along with a few beach runs, and was impressed at how well it kept the stuff outside from getting into my shoe.

The Wildfeel has a dual-density midsole, which means that it helps give you a feeling of moving forward when you're going up hills and absorbs impact when you’re going down.

Recent findings suggest that like many other Lululemon shoes, the toe box runs a little narrow. My heel slipped around a little when I first wore these shoes, although that’s pretty common in a trail shoe, and it got better with time and more wear.

Read More: Best Trail Running Shoes.

Recent findings suggest that there’s a wide range of shoes that consider themselves “stability” sneakers, but the Hoka Arahi 8 does a solid job correcting your stride with each step without being annoying. Many stability shoes are clunky and heavy, but the Arahi 8 manages to be lightweight at just 7.7 oz.

The Arahi 8 features a lot of changes from the previous version, the Arahi 7. This shoe uses special H-frame technology, featuring foam at the inner and outer foot, to deliver a more balanced support system. It’s roomy and comfortable, too. But this shoe is clearly not for everyone.

The level of stability is high, and that constant gait correction may feel like too much for some people. It also isn’t very responsive, so you’re not getting much back from your shoe with each stride other than security. (To be fair, though, that’s what people are usually after with a stability shoe.) Still, the Arahi 8 is impressively cushioned and very comfortable, whether you’re working your way through a long training session or just going out on a daily run.

Long runs require plenty of cushioning to support you along the way. The Nike Vomero Plus, which won the award for Best Cushioned Running Shoe in the 2026 Women’s Health Fitness Awards, is here to help. This shoe delivers a fun, bouncy feel that helps propel you as you rack up the miles.

Sources indicate that the Vomero Plus has a roomy toe box and overall comfortable feel, serving up a shoe that makes long runs a little more seamless. That bounciness comes courtesy of Nike’s ZoomX foam, which is positioned along the length of the shoe. The engineered upper is crafted from yarn for a soft, breathable sensation.

The Vomero Plus provides a grippy outsole, making it perfect for the pavement. But if you’re looking for a stability shoe, the Vomero Plus isn’t it. Its high heel stack and bounciness is too much for that. But if you want a highly cushioned feel as you log some serious miles, this is an excellent choice.

Sources indicate that the right race day shoe has the tough challenge of being supportive, cushiony, and lightweight, helping you to hit a PR without feeling like your footwear is holding you back. The Newly introduced Balance FuelCell SuperComp Elite v5 is designed with longer-distance racers (think: half and marathon runners) in mind, but can still be an excellent choice for 5Ks and 10Ks thanks to its lightweight (6 oz) construction and solid energy return.

In a recent development, let’s get this out of the way now: At $265, this is not a cheap shoe. With that, it’s unlikely to be a good investment for the occasional racer. But if your weekends are booked with road races, it’s worth at least considering.

Industry observers note that this shoe delivers a locked-in feel, along with great traction to give you more confidence, even over wet surfaces. The roomy toe box and breathable upper also reinforce the FuelCell SuperComp Elite v5’s comfortable feel. This shoe is stable without sacrificing punchiness, helping you to feel supported as you stride. Just be aware that the midfoot and heel may feel a little too narrow for those with wider feet. But, luckily, this sneaker is available in wide widths, too.

Read More: Best Running Shoes for Plantar Fasciitis.

The lululemon Beyondfeel running shoes truly live up to their name. They’re comfortable at the heels (and everywhere), with a heel stack that provides just the right amount of cushioning. It absorbs impact while still feeling responsive, especially during long runs. Plus, the cushioning around the ankle delivers security in every step.

The heel-to-toe drop is also a game changer—it really makes a difference for runners who heel-strike. Instead of feeling the usual jarring sensation from heel-striking, there are smooth transitions from each step. The bounce in the heel also makes it easier to maintain a steady stride without losing momentum, which is a huge benefit for runners who naturally land on their heels. The shoes guide feet to strike with the midfoot instead of the heel.

Industry observers note that these shoes feel slightly bouncy while you run, and offer decent grip for trails and roads, making for a versatile running shoe. If you’re an overpronator, this isn’t the shoe for you—it doesn’t provide enough medial support (on the inside of the shoe). But it’s got plenty of features to make running a dream for heel strikers.

Read More: Best lululemon Shoes Ranked.

There’s a range in severity with overpronators, and what works for one won’t work for everyone. But the Asics Gel-Nimbus 28 does a solid job trying to please everyone in the overpronation camp. This shoe delivers a feel that’s not too soft or too firm, giving you the support and stability you need without feeling like you’re in a “special” shoe.

This shoe is lightweight for a stability shoe at 8.5 oz, making it good for most runs that don’t involve speed work. It also delivers a solid, locked-in sensation to make you feel secure with each step. The shoe’s OrthoLite sockliner also supports that cozier feel. The Gel-Nimbus 28 feels slightly springy underfoot, which is rare for a stability shoe. (Still, the overall effect isn’t very responsive compared to non-stability shoes.).

According to recent reports, asics in general tends to run narrow and the Gel-Nimbus 28 is no exception. If your feet tend to teeter between regular and wide sizes, you may want to consider hedging your bets and trying out a larger size.

Sources indicate that the best shoe for speed work is very different from what you need for distance training or even race day. The Saucony Endorphin Azura is a lightweight (7.5 oz) shoe with a snappy feel that still manages to make you feel stable and locked in as you zip around.

Recent findings suggest that the Saucony Endorphin Azura uses Pebax foam to create a responsive, bouncy feel, making you feel a little faster than usual. It also has a wide and stable base for added security during training. While it’s designed for speed, you can still comfortably wear this sneaker for longer runs and daily mileage. Just be aware that the shoe’s special SpeedRoll technology may feel slightly awkward at slower speeds.

The Endorphin Azura’s outsole features XT-900 rubber for a grippy feel underfoot, making you feel comfortable pushing the pace. Saucony shoes are known for a narrower fit, and the Endorphin Azura is no exception. If you have wider feet, it may be best to look elsewhere. (It unfortunately doesn’t come in wide sizes.).

It has been revealed that maximum Cushioning: This type of cushion feels amazingly plush and has excellent shock absorption, which is essential for long-distance running. While they’re designed to minimize the impact on the joints, they’re not the best for speed workouts unless the shoe has a lower heel-to-toe drop and some firmness.

Medium: If you want to balance speed with stability, medium cushioning is ideal. Too much cushioning can cause runners with flat feet to overpronate more from the bulkiness and softness. So, this type of cushioning is best if you want a more aligned gait.

Sources indicate that this is the difference in height between the heel and front part (known as the forefoot) of the shoe. It can impact how your foot lands on the ground when you run. Low drops (0 to 4 mm) are flatter and encourage a natural running style where you land in the middle or front of your foot. They’re great if you like to feel close to the ground, enjoy trail running, or prefer a minimalist shoe design. Medium drop (5 to 8 mm) is a versatile option that offers mid-height and cushioning—this works well for most running styles. High drop (9 to 12 mm) tends to have more height in the heel to absorb impact (this is great for heel-strikers).

It has been revealed that this is the height of the cushion under the heel. It’s measured from the outsole (the bottom of the shoe) to the insole (where your foot rests). Higher stacks offer more softness for long-distance running or for those who need less impact on the joints. Prioritizing this means sacrificing ground feel, and for some, that may feel unbalanced given the additional height.

Running shoes can provide a slew of benefits to suit your feet, but podiatrists stress the importance of getting a well-fitting shoe. “The shoe should fit your foot well and not cause any rubbing on the toes,” claims Richard H. Graves, DPM, a podiatrist at Sol Foot & Ankle Centers in Long Beach, California “They should feel comfortable immediately upon putting them on and walking around.”.

Consider these areas of the shoe when checking the fit:.

Recent findings suggest that toe Box: This is the front part of the shoe where the toes sit. Toes spread naturally when you have extra room in the toe box, and this is especially vital during long runs since feet can swell. But if the toe box is too significant, it can lead to sliding and instability in the shoes.

It has been revealed that length: Since feet often swell from pounding pavement, it’s a good idea to have about a thumb’s width away from the tip of the shoe to your toe. If you’re unsure of your size, the best bet is to visit a running store to get properly fitted.

In a recent development, arch Support: Those with flat feet and overpronators (when your foot lands on your outside heel and rolls inward) will want to look for shoes with enough firmness and high arch support to help keep feet aligned. Too much cushioning can create an unbalanced feeling, which can further aggravate pain. Those with neutral to high arches will have no issues wearing shoes with neutral support. Most shoes specify which arch type they accommodate, so make sure to read their product descriptions. And, definitely don’t wear shoes with no arch support—your feet need support.

In a recent development, the type of running workouts you proposal to do will dictate elements like cushioning, support, and weight. More cushioning is often better with daily training and distance runs. You may also get away with a slightly heavier (but not too heavy) shoe, which usually means there’s more cushioning and stability. But shoes for speed work and race day tend to have less cushioning and a lighter weight, making it easier to move faster. For a deep-dive into the topic of running shoe selection, check out our story about how to figure out which type of running shoe you need.

It has been revealed that A stability shoe can help correct gait issues like overpronation, which is when your foot rolls inward excessively when you run or walk. Not everyone needs a stability shoe, but some level of stability is important for reducing injury risk when you’re an overpronator. There are a few ways to tell if you overpronate, per Graves: Your feet appear to be rolling inward when you stand in a relaxed position and the heels of shoes you’ve worn are tilted inward.

It has been revealed that you should switch out your running shoes every 300 to 500 miles. An easy way to maximize your shoe lifespan is to have a few pairs that you rotate between runs. Also, if you visually see them degrading, it's time to snag a new pair.

Sources indicate that running shoes can be washed in cold water in the washing machine with light detergent, or spot-cleaned with a sponge. But, you should never put your shoes in the dryer—they can shrink! Instead, let them air dry in the sun.

A simple at-home way to determine your arch type is the wet footprint test. You simply dip your foot in the water and step onto paper. If you see your entire foot, you have flat feet. Your foot will look like a comma if you have high arches, while a neutral arch will show slight elevation.

I’ve tested dozens of pairs of running shoes to determine which make the cut for the best running shoes for women. As a personal trainer, fitness writer, and runner with years of experience testing running shoes, I put each pair to the test during two-mile runs where I evaluated key performance factors such as cushioning, stability, comfort, support, traction, and responsiveness. I also considered how well the shoes supported my stride and whether or not they helped me maintain a consistent pace. Additionally, WH fitness editors provided feedback on select shoes they love to wear during training and racing.

#64307. Here are the coolest e-motorcycles and gear we saw at EICMA 2026

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (2050 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Here are the coolest e-motorcycles and gear we saw at EICMA 2026

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2050 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every year, the world’s largest motorcycle companies (and plenty of the world’s smallest motorcycle companies, too) converge on Milan, Italy for Europe’s premier motorcycle showcase.
  • Below is a list of the best things I saw while walking around the show this year, presented in no particular order.
  • LiveWire came to EICMA with perhaps its most diverse electric two-wheeler lineup yet, showing just how far the company has expanded beyond the premium electric motorcycles that originally defined the Harley-Davidson spin-off.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every year, the world’s largest motorcycle companies (and plenty of the world’s smallest motorcycle companies, too) converge on Milan, Italy for Europe’s premier motorcycle showcase. That means that all of the newest electric motorcycle announcements happen in one place, and we get a chance to check out the coolest developments and most interesting newly introduced gear.

Below is a list of the best things I saw while walking around the show this year, presented in no particular order.

LiveWire came to EICMA with perhaps its most diverse electric two-wheeler lineup yet, showing just how far the company has expanded beyond the premium electric motorcycles that originally defined the Harley-Davidson spin-off.

The upcoming S4 Honcho family was a major focus, including the street-oriented Honcho Street, off-road Honcho Trail, and newly unveiled Honcho Skate, a stripped-down addition to the modular platform. The booth also included LiveWire’s larger S2 electric motorcycles, creating a pretty broad spectrum from lightweight urban machines up through full-size highway-capable electric motorcycles.

The other massive piece of the booth was DUST Moto, which LiveWire acquired earlier this year. The production-intent DUST Hightail was displayed alongside the newly revealed DUST Spur, giving LiveWire an immediate presence in the increasingly popular lightweight electric dirt bike category.

Add in STACYC’s electric balance bikes for young riders, and the entire booth almost looked like an electric two-wheeler progression chart: start a kid on a STACYC, move up through lightweight DUST and Honcho machines, and eventually graduate to a full-size LiveWire.

Recent findings suggest that GR1T Motorcycles is a relatively young European electric motorcycle startup that caught my eye at EICMA with its G1 platform, a lightweight electric motorcycle designed and engineered in Italy. The basic recipe is pretty compelling: 130 km/h (81 mph) top speed, 11 kW of continuous power and 26.6 kW (36 hp) peak, all while weighing just 130 kg (287 lb).

In a recent development, perhaps most importantly for urban riders, its roughly 6 kWh battery is actually split into two removable 3 kWh packs, meaning apartment dwellers can pull the batteries out and charge them inside. They’re big, but removing them is doable.

GR1T’s bikes therefore pack in around 50% more battery capacity than most electric motorcycles in this size and weight class, meaning roughly 50% more range, as well.

There are also some interesting and clever design choices, like the underslung rear suspension and the triple-camera system that includes front and rear dashcams plus a cockpit-facing camera for recording the rider.

The clever part of the overall design scheme is that GR1T isn’t developing a separate platform for every motorcycle. The same basic G1 chassis, motor, batteries, belt drive, and electronics underpin four versions: the G1S Street, G1X Scrambler, G1XR Raider, and utility-oriented G1M Mission.

Prices are set to start at €8,495 including VAT, putting these squarely in that emerging category of reasonably affordable, lightweight electric motorcycles that have enough speed for real-world commuting without chasing superbike performance.

There’s an important caveat, though: these aren’t production motorcycles yet. GR1T says it is presently fundraising, with factory development and pre-orders set to follow after funding closes and first deliveries now targeted for the first half of 2028.

So the bikes aren’t quite ready for primetime yet, but it’s definitely a company to watch.

Real Motors brought one of the more visually striking electric motorcycles to EICMA with Project: ARES, a futuristic electric café racer that the American startup describes as an “Electric Analog” machine – basically an attempt to preserve the raw, mechanical connection of motorcycling while ditching unnecessary screens and gadgetry.

And there’s plenty of performance underneath the sci-fi bodywork: Real Motors lists a 75 kW (100 hp) motor, a 15 kWh battery, a 120 mph (192 km/h) top speed, and an estimated weight of 485 lb (220 kg).

Sources indicate that the analog analogy is spot on, with the display probably the simplest and most straightforward I’ve ever seen on an electric motorcycle. There’s also no app, no subscription, and no digital handcuffs. The bike is very much the electric equivalent of a simple ICE bike that just rides, albeit with a much nicer ride.

Unlike many of the futuristic concepts scattered around EICMA, ARES is actually headed toward limited production.

Real Motors prepares to build just 250 examples in its first LOT 01 production run, with pricing starting at $20,000 and North American deliveries targeted for early 2027. European deliveries are expected after homologation is completed.

The organization has also brought former LiveWire CTO Vance Strader onto the project as it makes the difficult transition from a very cool prototype into an actual production motorcycle.

I actually had the chance to do a spin on the bike, and so I’ll be reporting back on the experience. But you can tell from my smile below that the ride was quite an experience!

Seatylock has been my go-to e-bike lock organization for several years now, and I use their locks for my several e-bikes and my wife’s e-bike too.

Now Seatylock has returned with some even more impressive locks. The company showed off its new Ultra D28 lock, which is both angle grinder-proof and wide enough to lock the wheel of a motorcycle. It solves the problem of how do you make a lock strong enough for a motorcycle but also small and light enough that you can actually carry it with you, unlike a massive chain lock that usually stays where you park your motorcycle overnight.

In the image below, you can see the shackle next to an exposed section demonstrating the diamond coating that essentially destroys angle grinder discs – even diamond coated discs.

The company also has a slightly smaller version of the same lock designed for bicycles.

Recent findings suggest that both will absolutely destroy even the toughest angle grinder discs. Sure, eventually someone could cut through them, but it may take a dozen discs and by that point the thief has moved on to an easier target.

At EICMA 2026, Royal Enfield continued expanding its electric motorcycle ambitions with its Flying Flea sub-brand, showcasing the scrambler-style motorcycle alongside its growing lineup of lightweight, retro-inspired electric motorcycles.

There were several interesting colorways and customized designs on display, showcasing the Flying Flea’s stylish design.

The new models blend Royal Enfield’s classic design heritage with modern electric technology, targeting urban riders and those looking for a fun, approachable electric motorcycle rather than a high-performance machine.

With distinctive styling, compact proportions, and an emphasis on accessible riding, the Flying Flea lineup represents Royal Enfield’s effort to carve out a place in the emerging market for smaller electric motorcycles while maintaining the character that has made its gasoline-powered bikes so popular.

Yamaha showed off its newly introduced NMAX E electric scooter, bringing battery-powered performance to one of the brand’s most recognizable urban scooter families.

Designed as an electric alternative to the popular gasoline-powered NMAX, the fresh model combines familiar sporty styling with a quiet, low-maintenance electric drivetrain aimed at everyday city commuting.

The NMAX E uses Yamaha’s newly introduced compact eAxle powertrain, shared with the larger-wheeled XENTER E, and delivers up to 7.5 kW (10 hp) of peak power, putting it in the 125cc-equivalent class.

With its practical step-through design, automatic operation, and approachable performance, the NMAX E represents another step in Yamaha’s push to electrify its urban mobility lineup, particularly in European markets where scooters are already a popular alternative to cars.

Segway showed off a upcoming vision for safer electric scooters, including its futuristic X Cruiser concept that takes rider protection to a whole new level.

Rather than relying solely on traditional motorcycle safety equipment, the X Cruiser explores automotive-inspired features such as integrated seats with seatbelts, partial enclosures, and even a fully roofed version designed to offer additional protection from the elements.

Recent findings suggest that the concept includes several configurations, ranging from a more conventional open scooter to a partially enclosed design and a fully covered model that looks like a cross between a motorcycle and a tiny electric car. While these designs are still concepts rather than production-ready scooters, they demonstrate how Segway is rethinking two-wheeled transportation by exploring ways to make electric scooters safer, more comfortable, and potentially more appealing to riders who might otherwise be hesitant to trade four wheels for two.

Eli Electric Vehicles took to EICMA 2026 to display its compact Eli Zero electric quadricycle, a tiny two-seat urban EV designed to offer much of the convenience of a car without the size, weight, or expense of a conventional automobile.

With its enclosed cabin, side-by-side seating, and ultra-compact footprint, the Eli Zero offers a practical alternative to larger vehicles for short city trips, combining the weather protection and comfort of a car with the maneuverability and efficiency of a much smaller vehicle.

In a recent development, the tech giant revealed a more powerful L7e-class version of the Eli Zero that it had previously teased, expanding the vehicle’s capabilities beyond its existing L6e configuration. The new Race Edition also pushes the envelope farther with custom interior and a few extra accents to the body.

With growing interest in smaller, more efficient urban transportation, Eli’s presence at EICMA definitely underlined how the show is increasingly embracing electric mobility solutions that go beyond traditional motorcycles and scooters.

According to recent reports, NIU indicated off its latest lineup of electric scooters, continuing the brand’s push to make battery-powered two-wheelers a practical alternative to gasoline-powered urban transportation. Known for its sleek designs, connected technology, and approachable electric scooters, NIU highlighted models aimed at a range of riders, from everyday city commuters to those looking for more powerful machines capable of keeping up with faster urban traffic.

The firm showed off several new models for the 2027 model year, with scooters that combine modern styling with features such as smartphone connectivity, smart security systems, and efficient electric drivetrains, all while maintaining the simplicity and low operating costs that make electric scooters so appealing.

While I didn’t see anything groundbreaking at the brand’s booth this year, the incremental updates look to push fresh tech features further throughout the brand’s many models, helping more of NIU’s offerings enter that premium level that the tech giant has been known for.

For something a bit wilder, Honda shared its futuristic EV Outlier Concept, an electric motorcycle that explores what two-wheeled design could look like when engineers are freed from the constraints of traditional gasoline-powered motorcycles.

Recent findings suggest that with its long, low-slung profile, radically different riding position, and futuristic bodywork, the EV Outlier looks more like something out of a science fiction movie than a conventional motorcycle. The concept features electric motors integrated into both wheels, giving it two-wheel drive while opening up newly introduced possibilities for packaging and weight distribution.

Rather than simply replacing a combustion engine with a battery and motor, Honda used the EV Outlier to rethink the entire motorcycle layout, demonstrating how electrification could lead to entirely newly introduced types of riding experiences.

While the bike remains a design concept with no confirmed production looks, it offers an intriguing glimpse into Honda’s vision for the future of electric motorcycles.

It has been revealed that vespa showed off its next-generation electric scooter lineup at EICMA, including electric versions of the Primavera, Sprint S, and Primavera Tech. While they don’t look radically different, there’s a lot more happening underneath the familiar steel bodywork.

A latest Italian-made, rare-earth-free electric motor improves efficiency and performance, while the 45 km/h Primavera and Sprint S now feature removable batteries.

The faster 67 km/h Primavera Tech gets up to 90 km of WMTC range – a 12.5% improvement – along with an updated vehicle management system and more efficient charger.
